# Firebase Architecture

**Status:** Draft v8 — 5 Nov 2026. v8: Phase 5B — `reports` and `operations` shapes and rules, Storage rule for report files, surgery-day and post-op appointments regenerated by the client, doctor edits of visit-type defaults, `visits.operationId` set by the new-visit form. v7: Phase 5A — `prescriptions` shape and rules (own visit, same Karachi day), follow-up `appointments` written in the prescription batch, `appointments` rules opened, doctor summary by aggregate queries with its composite index, today's-visits listener scoped to the doctor for doctor-only sessions. v6: Phase 4 — `visits` shape and rules (reception and own doctor may change status), client token from the cached today's visits, one shared today's-visits listener behind the queue, list, summary and sync badge, receipt data denormalised on the visit. v5: Phase 3 — `families`, `patients` rules and shape; `assignPatientNo` and `checkDuplicateFamilyPhone` triggers; `dobApproximate` instead of `ageYears`; patient cache listeners; seed family. v4: Phase 2 — `branches`, `settings`, `departments`, `visitTypes`, `doctors` rules; doctor–login link kept by `createUser` / `setUserRoles`; logo in Storage; first-run setup from the app. v3: budget decisions — summaries kept by increments (no recompute), no backup, Storage bucket in us-central1, no prescription photos, cost table for 500 visits a day.
**Companion to:** [FEATURES.md](FEATURES.md). Feature behaviour is defined there; this document defines how it is stored and secured.

---

## 1. Decisions

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Firebase project | One new project, Blaze plan. No separate dev project; test data is created and cleaned by hand before go-live. |
| Region | `asia-south1` (Mumbai) for Firestore and Functions, closest region to Pakistan. Storage bucket in `us-central1`, because Firebase's no-cost Storage quota (5 GB stored, 1 GB download a day) applies only to US buckets. |
| Structure | Top-level collections. Every record carries `branchId`. One branch document exists today. |
| Auth | Firebase Auth, email and password. Roles stored in custom claims and mirrored in the user document. Admin creates users through a Cloud Function. |
| Patient ID | `YY-NNNNN`, e.g. `26-00341`. Assigned by a Cloud Function on sync. Offline, a temporary ID `T-XXXXX` is shown. |
| Token | Department code plus daily sequence per doctor, e.g. `E-12`, `H-5`. Resets at midnight Asia/Karachi. Generated on the client. |
| Visit types | Each belongs to one department. |
| Appointments | Date plus free-text time. No slot grid, no working hours. |
| Deletes | Soft delete with reason. `deleted: true` hides the record from lists and totals. |
| Dashboard | Reads only `dailySummaries`. A Cloud Function applies the difference of every visit, sale, expense or patient write to that day's summary with `FieldValue.increment`. No reads, no recompute. An Admin "Recompute day" button repairs a single day if a total ever drifts. |
| Inventory | No batch or expiry tracking. Suppliers and purchase bills are tracked; a purchase creates an expense. |
| Payouts | Admin chooses any date range. Payout = salary amount entered by Admin (prefilled with monthly salary) plus share of fees in the range. |
| Family rules | Patient may have a personal phone. Patient can be moved between families. Family phone can be changed. |
| Patient age | Decided 4 Nov 2026. Only `dateOfBirth` is stored. An age typed by reception becomes 1 January of the birth year with `dobApproximate: true`; the UI shows `~40 y`. No `ageYears` field. |
| Family phone clash | Decided 4 Nov 2026. The client refuses to create a family, or change a family phone, to a number another family has (query on `families.phone`, from the cache when offline). A clash that slips through offline is flagged by `checkDuplicateFamilyPhone`. |
| Queue | Doctor sees only their own queue. |
| Timezone | Asia/Karachi for day boundaries. |
| Backup | None in v1 (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, cost). Firestore replicates data across zones; the risk accepted is accidental bulk deletion or corruption by the app, which soft deletes and Admin-only edits mitigate. Point-in-time recovery or a monthly export can be enabled later without code changes. |
| Reminders | No reminders collection. The "due today" list is a query over appointments. Sent state is stored on the appointment. |
| Doctor ↔ login link | Decided 3 Nov 2026. `users.doctorId` and `doctors.userId` are both written by the user-management functions in one transaction; the doctor form and rules never touch `doctors.userId`. One login per doctor. |
| WhatsApp placeholders | `{patient}`, `{doctor}`, `{date}`, `{time}`, `{clinic}` in `settings.whatsappTemplates`. |
| Prescription edits | Decided 5 Nov 2026. A prescription may be created and updated only by the doctor of its visit, and updated only while `request.time` is before the end of the prescription's Karachi day (`date` + 1 day at 00:00 Karachi = `date` 19:00 UTC, computed in rules from the stored `date`). No Admin edit path in v1. |
| Operation appointments | Decided 5 Nov 2026. Scheduling writes the operation, one `source: operation` appointment on the surgery date and one `source: postOp` appointment per post-op day in a single batch. Changing the date or the days cancels the affected appointments and creates new ones in one batch; cancelling the operation cancels them all. Appointment IDs are kept on the operation. |
| Report files | Decided 5 Nov 2026. PDF, JPEG, PNG up to 10 MB; images shrunk on the client (1200 px, JPEG 80) behind an `ImageShrinker` abstraction. Upload first, then the document. Soft delete by reception or Admin with a reason. |
| Doctor summary | Decided 5 Nov 2026. Counts and money per period come from Firestore aggregate queries (`count`, `sum`) over `visits` filtered by `doctorId`, `status == completed`, `deleted == false` and a `date` range: one billed read per period, server only. |
| Patient cache | Decided 5 Nov 2026, replacing the full-collection listeners. Reception devices are **local-first**: every patient search asks the Firestore cache first (free) and goes to the server only when the cache has no match; the documents the server returns stay in the cache. Nothing is downloaded up front. A `PatientSyncController` keeps the cached set fresh with **delta pulls**: on the first run it records the newest `updatedAt` of `patients` and `families` as watermarks (one read each), then at sign-in and every 5 minutes it reads only documents with `updatedAt >= watermark` (pages of 500, server only) and advances the watermark. A search footer "Not here? Search online" forces a server search. Functions that touch patients or families (`assignPatientNo`, `checkDuplicateFamilyPhone`) bump `updatedAt` so the pull sees their writes. Web uses the multi-tab persistent cache and asks the browser for durable storage (`navigator.storage.persist()`). Reason: Firestore bills a listener disconnected for more than 30 minutes as a brand-new query, so the old full listeners re-read every patient on each morning's reconnect, and the searches were server reads although the data was cached. |

---

## 2. Services Used

| Service | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Firestore | All application data. Offline persistence enabled on reception web. |
| Authentication | Email/password login, custom claims for roles. |
| Cloud Storage | Report files and the clinic logo. Bucket in `us-central1` for the no-cost quota. |
| Cloud Functions (2nd gen, TypeScript, Node 22) | User management, patient number assignment, incremental daily summaries, audit log. |
| Hosting | Reception and Admin web app. |
| App Check | Enabled for web and mobile to block requests from outside the app. |

---

## 3. Conventions

- Document IDs are Firestore auto-IDs unless stated.
- `branchId` on every business document. Default branch ID is `main`.
- Dates that mean "a clinic day" are stored as strings `YYYY-MM-DD` computed in Asia/Karachi, so they are queryable and unambiguous offline.
- Timestamps use `createdAt: serverTimestamp()` plus `createdAtLocal` (client clock) because `serverTimestamp` is null in the local cache until sync.
- Money is stored as integer PKR. No decimals.
- Names denormalised onto visits (`patientName`, `doctorName`, `visitTypeName`) so lists and receipts need one read and keep history even if the source is renamed.
- Fields `deleted`, `deletedAt`, `deletedBy`, `deleteReason` appear on any soft-deletable document. Queries always filter `deleted == false`.
- `searchKeys` is an array of lowercase prefixes used for name search (first 3 to 12 characters of each word) because Firestore has no substring search.

---

## 4. Collections

### 4.1 `branches/{branchId}`
```
name, address, phone, active, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
`branches/main` is created by the first-run setup with the clinic name, address and phone.

### 4.2 `settings/general`  (single document)
```
clinicName, logoUrl, address, phone, receiptFooter,
defaultReceiptCopies: 1,
followUpReminderDays: 0,
reminders: { appointment: true, followUp: true, postOp: true },
whatsappTemplates: { appointment: "...", followUp: "...", postOp: "...", adhoc: "..." },
timezone: "Asia/Karachi",
updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Created by the first-run setup (§10) with default templates; `logoUrl` is set by the logo upload (§7). `followUpReminderDays` is 0 to 30, `defaultReceiptCopies` 1 to 5. Templates use the placeholders in §1. The app keeps one listener on this document per signed-in session for the header name and the first-run banner.

### 4.3 `users/{uid}`
ID is the Auth UID.
```
email, displayName, roles: ["reception" | "doctor" | "admin"],
doctorId (nullable), active, branchIds: ["main"],
mustChangePassword, createdAt, createdBy
```
Roles are also written to Auth custom claims `{ roles: [...], doctorId, branchIds }` by the `setUserRoles` function. Security rules read claims, not this document.

### 4.4 `departments/{departmentId}`
```
name: "Eye", code: "E", sortOrder, active, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Seeded with Eye (`eye`, `E`) and Homeopathy (`homeo`, `H`) by the first-run setup, fixed IDs. `code` is 1 to 3 letters, unique (checked by the Admin form), and prefixes tokens. Changing a code rewrites `departmentCode` on the department's doctors in the same batch (decided 3 Nov 2026).

### 4.5 `doctors/{doctorId}`
```
userId, name, departmentId, departmentCode, specialisation,
salary (monthly PKR), sharePercent, shareBasis: "gross" | "net",
fees: { [visitTypeId]: amount },        // fee schedule embedded
active, branchId, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Fee schedule is a map on the doctor so reception loads one document per doctor. `sharePercent` is a number 0 to 100 (decimals allowed). `userId` is the login link, written only by `createUser` / `setUserRoles` (§5); the fee grid rewrites the whole `fees` map of one doctor per save. Fee changes are audited by the `auditDoctors` trigger (Phase 9).

### 4.6 `visitTypes/{visitTypeId}`
```
departmentId, name, isOperation, isFollowUp, sortOrder, active,
defaultPreOpChecklist: [ { id, label } ],     // operation types only
defaultPostOpDays: [1, 7, 30],                 // operation types only
createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Each department is seeded with Checkup and Follow-up (`isFollowUp: true`), fixed IDs `eye-checkup`, `eye-follow-up`, `homeo-checkup`, `homeo-follow-up`. Eye also gets Eye Test (`eye-eye-test`). Operation types are added by Admin; `isOperation` and `isFollowUp` are exclusive. Checklist item IDs are client UUIDs; post-op days are 1 to 365, kept sorted.

### 4.7 `families/{familyId}`
```
phone ("03001234567", normalised), headName, address, patientCount,
duplicatePhone (false; set by checkDuplicateFamilyPhone only),
branchId, createdAt, createdAtLocal, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
`phone` is indexed and unique in practice (checked on client before create; a Function flags duplicates created offline). `patientCount` is kept by the client batches that add or move patients.

### 4.8 `patients/{patientId}`
```
patientNo (null until assigned, e.g. "26-00341"),
tempNo ("T-7K3M9": T- plus five characters from A-Z, 2-9 without 0/O/1/I),
familyId, name, gender ("male" | "female" | "other"),
dateOfBirth ("YYYY-MM-DD", nullable), dobApproximate (bool, see §1),
personalPhone (nullable),
phones: [familyPhone, personalPhone],   // denormalised for array-contains search
address, notes, searchKeys: [],
visitCount, lastVisitAt, lastDoctorId,
deleted, deletedAt, deletedBy, deleteReason,
branchId, createdAt, createdAtLocal, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Moving a patient to another family updates `familyId` and `phones`, and adjusts `patientCount` on both families in one batch. Changing a family phone fans out to `phones` on every patient of that family (client batch, families are small). Searches filter `deleted` on the client and sort by name in memory (result sets are small), so the Phase 3 queries need no composite index. `updatedAt` is the delta-sync watermark field for both `patients` and `families` (§9): every client write stamps it with `serverTimestamp()` and the two Functions below do the same, so the sync query `where updatedAt >= watermark orderBy updatedAt, __name__` needs only the automatic single-field index.

### 4.9 `counters/{counterId}`
```
patients_2026: { value: 341 }
```
Only Cloud Functions write here. Tokens do not use counters.

### 4.10 `appointments/{appointmentId}`
```
patientId, patientName, patientNo, phone,
doctorId, doctorName, departmentId,
date ("YYYY-MM-DD"), time ("10:30" or ""), 
source: "manual" | "followUp" | "postOp" | "operation",
operationId (nullable), prescriptionId (nullable),
status: "booked" | "arrived" | "cancelled" | "noShow",
visitId (set when arrived),
reminderSentAt (nullable), reminderSentBy (nullable),
notes, branchId, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt
```
Follow-ups from a prescription and post-op follow-ups are appointments with `source` set and `time` empty. The reminders-due-today screen is three queries over this collection.

Phase 5B (decided 5 Nov 2026): scheduling an operation writes a `source: "operation"` appointment on `scheduledDate` (notes = the operation type name, `operationId` set) and a `source: "postOp"` appointment per post-op day (`date` = scheduledDate + day), all `status: "booked"`, `time: ""`. The operation keeps `surgeryAppointmentId` and `followUpAppointmentIds`.

Phase 5A writes the follow-up appointment in the same batch as the prescription (decided 5 Nov 2026): `source: "followUp"`, `prescriptionId` = the visit ID, `status: "booked"`, patient and doctor names copied from the visit, `date` = the follow-up date, `time: ""`, `notes: ""`, `operationId: null`, `visitId: null`, `reminderSentAt: null`. Changing the follow-up date updates that appointment's `date`; clearing it sets `status: "cancelled"`; setting it again after clearing creates a new appointment. The prescription keeps the ID in `followUpAppointmentId`.

### 4.11 `visits/{visitId}`
```
patientId, patientName, patientNo, phone, familyId,
doctorId, doctorName, departmentId, departmentCode,
visitTypeId, visitTypeName, isOperation, isFollowUp,
token: 12, tokenLabel: "E-12",
date ("YYYY-MM-DD"), createdAt, createdAtLocal,
isFirstVisit,                            // true when the patient had visitCount 0 at creation; feeds newPatients
fee, discountAmount, discountReason, netAmount,
paymentMethod: "cash" | "bank" | "jazzcash" | "easypaisa", paymentRef,
status: "waiting" | "inProgress" | "completed",
startedAt, completedAt,
appointmentId, operationId (set by the new-visit form when the patient has a scheduled operation of the chosen operation type, decided 5 Nov 2026), saleId, hasPrescription,
receiptCopies,
deleted: false, deletedAt, deletedBy, deleteReason, editReason,
branchId, createdBy
```
Visits are written by reception (and Admin) and only edited by Admin, except `status`, `startedAt`, `completedAt`, which reception and the assigned doctor may update (decided 4 Nov 2026: reception drives the queue for doctors who do not use the app), and `hasPrescription`, which only the assigned doctor sets (Phase 5). Rules enforce this field by field.

Create shape (Phase 4): `patientName`, `doctorName`, `visitTypeName`, `tokenLabel`, `date` non-empty strings; `token` int ≥ 1; `fee` int ≥ 0; `discountAmount` int between 0 and `fee`; `discountReason` non-empty when `discountAmount > 0`; `netAmount == fee - discountAmount`; `paymentMethod` in cash/bank/jazzcash/easypaisa; `status == "waiting"`; `deleted == false`; `receiptCopies` int 1 to 5; `branchId` in the caller's claims; `createdBy` the caller. `discountReason` is one of the preset labels or the free text typed under Other (FEATURES §2). `isFirstVisit` is `patient.visitCount == 0` at creation. The same batch updates the patient: `visitCount` increment, `lastVisitAt` (client clock, so it is visible offline), `lastDoctorId`.

**Token generation (client):** query the local cache (`Source.cache`) for `visits` where `doctorId == X and date == today`, take `max(token) + 1`, label with the doctor's `departmentCode`. The cache holds today's visits because the reception session keeps the today's-visits listener open (§9). Single reception device, so no conflict handling in v1.

### 4.12 `prescriptions/{visitId}`
ID equals the visit ID. Separate from the visit so doctor writes never collide with reception writes. Typed only; there is no photo mode.
```
visitId, patientId, patientName, patientNo, doctorId, doctorName, departmentId, date,
eye: { od: { sph, cyl, axis, add, va }, os: { sph, cyl, axis, add, va } },  // Eye only, else null
homeo: [ { medicine, potency, dosage, duration } ],                          // Homeo only, else []
diagnosis, advice,
followUpDate (nullable), followUpAppointmentId (nullable),
branchId, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
Eye values are stored as the normalised strings the doctor typed (`"-1.25"`, `"+1.00"`, `"90"`, `"6/6"`), empty when not measured; the client validates SPH and CYL as 0.25 steps, AXIS as 0 to 180 and ADD as a positive 0.25 step. Departments other than `eye` and `homeo` store diagnosis and advice only. The save batch (Phase 5A, decided 5 Nov 2026) sets the prescription, sets `visits.hasPrescription = true` (plus `status: completed` and `completedAt` when the doctor presses Complete) and creates or updates the follow-up appointment (§4.10). One `commitOrQueue` per save.

### 4.13 `reports/{reportId}`
```
patientId, patientName, visitId (nullable), title, fileName,
storagePath, downloadUrl, mimeType, sizeBytes,
uploadedBy, uploadedAt, branchId,
deleted, deletedAt, deletedBy, deleteReason, updatedAt, updatedBy
```
`storagePath` is `patients/{patientId}/reports/{reportId}.{pdf|jpg|png}` (§7); the document ID is chosen on the client before the upload so the file and the record share it. `mimeType` in application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png; `sizeBytes` ≤ 10 MB after the client resize. Reads filter `deleted` on the client (one `patientId` query, no composite index).

### 4.14 `operations/{operationId}`
```
patientId, patientName, patientNo, phone, visitId, visitTypeId, visitTypeName,
surgeonDoctorId, surgeonName, departmentId, scheduledById,
scheduledDate, status: "scheduled" | "done" | "cancelled",
checklist: [ { id, label, done, doneBy, doneAt } ],   // copied from visit type, patient items may be added
checklistComplete,                                       // kept in step with checklist by the client; rules read it
checklistOverrideReason (nullable),
postOpDays: [1, 7, 30],                                 // copied from visit type, editable
surgeryAppointmentId (nullable), followUpAppointmentIds: [],
doneAt, doneBy, cancelReason (nullable),
notes, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy, branchId
```
When `scheduledDate` is set or `postOpDays` changes, the client regenerates the appointments (cancels old, creates new) in one batch (§4.10). `status` moves scheduled → done (all checklist items ticked, or `checklistOverrideReason` set) or scheduled → cancelled (`cancelReason`, appointments cancelled). The doctor's operations list is one `surgeonDoctorId` query filtered and sorted on the client (no composite index yet). Doctors update their department's operation-type defaults (`defaultPreOpChecklist`, `defaultPostOpDays`) directly on `visitTypes` (rules limit them to those two fields).

### 4.15 `inventoryItems/{itemId}`
```
category: "medicine" | "frame" | "lens" | "consumable",
name, brand, unit, purchasePrice, salePrice,
stock, lowStockThreshold,
lens: { type: "singleVision" | "bifocal" | "progressive", sph, cyl },   // lens only
lensKey: "singleVision|-1.25|-0.50",                                      // lens only, unique per power
searchKeys, active, branchId, createdAt, updatedAt
```
Stock is changed only with `FieldValue.increment` inside a batch that also writes a `stockMovements` document. This stays correct offline.

### 4.16 `suppliers/{supplierId}`
```
name, phone, address, notes, active, createdAt
```

### 4.17 `purchases/{purchaseId}`
```
supplierId, supplierName, billNo, date,
items: [ { itemId, name, qty, unitCost, lineTotal } ],
total, note, expenseId, createdBy, createdAt, branchId
```
Client batch: create purchase, one `stockMovements` per line, increment each item's `stock`, create an `expenses` document with `source: "purchase"`.

### 4.18 `stockMovements/{movementId}`
```
itemId, itemName, qty (positive in, negative out),
type: "purchase" | "sale" | "operationUse" | "adjustment",
refId (purchaseId | saleId | operationId), reason,
createdBy, createdAt, branchId
```

### 4.19 `sales/{saleId}`
```
patientId (nullable), patientName, visitId (nullable), date,
items: [ { itemId, name, category, qty, unitPrice, lineTotal, lensKey } ],
subtotal, discountAmount, discountReason, total,
paymentMethod, paymentRef,
deleted, deletedAt, deletedBy, deleteReason,
createdBy, createdAt, createdAtLocal, branchId
```

### 4.20 `expenses/{expenseId}`
```
category: "rent" | "salary" | "utilities" | "supplies" | "purchase" | "payout" | "other",
amount, date, note,
source: "manual" | "purchase" | "payout", refId,
deleted, createdBy, createdAt, branchId
```

### 4.21 `payouts/{payoutId}`
```
doctorId, doctorName, periodStart, periodEnd,
salaryAmount, grossFees, discounts, netFees,
shareBasis, sharePercent, shareAmount, total,
paid, paidAt, paidBy, expenseId, note, createdAt, branchId
```
Fees in range are computed by the client from `dailySummaries.byDoctor` for the days in the period.

### 4.22 `dailySummaries/{YYYY-MM-DD}`
Written only by the `applyDailySummaryDelta` function, with `FieldValue.increment` on every field. Missing documents are created by the first increment.
```
date, branchId,
visits, newPatients, returningPatients,
grossFees, discounts, netFees,
byPayment: { cash, bank, jazzcash, easypaisa },
byDepartment: { [departmentId]: { visits, gross, discounts, net } },
byDoctor: { [doctorId]: { visits, gross, discounts, net } },
discountsByUser: { [uid]: { count, amount } },
discountsByReason: { [reason]: { count, amount } },
salesTotal, salesDiscounts, salesByCategory: { medicine, frame, lens, consumable },
expensesTotal, expensesByCategory: {},
netProfit,
updatedAt
```
Dashboard ranges sum these documents. A month is at most 31 reads.

**Delta rule.** For each write the function computes the document's contribution before and after (zero when absent or `deleted: true`) and increments the summary by the difference. A visit contributes `visits: 1`, `grossFees: fee`, `discounts: discountAmount`, `netFees: netAmount`, its payment method, department and doctor buckets, discount by user and reason, and `newPatients` or `returningPatients` from `isFirstVisit`. A sale contributes to the sales fields, an expense to the expense fields, and `netProfit` is `netFees + salesTotal - expensesTotal`. Status-only changes produce a zero delta and are skipped. Firestore triggers can fire twice for one write; the `eventId` is stored in `summaryEvents/{eventId}` with a 2-day TTL and the increment is skipped if it already exists, which keeps the totals exact.

### 4.23 `summaryEvents/{eventId}`
Written only by `applyDailySummaryDelta`. Idempotency ledger: `{ date, appliedAt, expiresAt }` with a Firestore TTL policy on `expiresAt` (2 days).

### 4.24 `auditLogs/{logId}`
Written only by Cloud Functions.
```
collection, docId, action: "create" | "update" | "delete",
userId, userName, reason,
before: {}, after: {}, changedFields: [],
createdAt
```
Audited collections: `visits`, `sales`, `expenses`, `doctors`, `visitTypes`, `inventoryItems` (stock and prices), `users`, `settings`, `payouts`. The acting user is taken from `updatedBy` on the document, which rules force to equal `request.auth.uid`.

---

## 5. Cloud Functions

| Function | Trigger | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `createUser` | callable, Admin only | Input `{ email, displayName, roles, doctorId?, temporaryPassword }` (min 8 chars; `doctorId` required when roles include doctor). With a `doctorId`, first checks `doctors/{doctorId}` exists (`not-found`) and is not linked to another login (`already-exists`). Creates the Auth user, sets claims `{ roles, doctorId, branchIds: ["main"] }`, writes `users/{uid}` with `mustChangePassword: true`, then sets `doctors/{doctorId}.userId = uid` in a transaction. Email is trimmed and lower-cased. Duplicate email → `already-exists`. If any later step fails the Auth user and doc are deleted again. Returns `{ uid }`. |
| `setUserRoles` | callable, Admin only | Input `{ uid, roles?, doctorId?, displayName?, active? }`. Before touching the account, syncs the doctor link in one transaction: the new doctor (if any) must exist and be unlinked or linked to this uid, gets `userId = uid`; the previous doctor of this uid gets `userId = null`. Then updates custom claims and the user doc (`branchIds` kept, `updatedAt/By` written), also writes `displayName` to the Auth profile. `active: false` disables the Auth account and revokes refresh tokens; `active: true` re-enables. Rejects an admin removing their own admin role or deactivating themselves (`failed-precondition`). Granting `doctor` requires a `doctorId`. |
| `createTestAdmin` | callable, **anyone**, only while `ALLOW_TEST_ADMIN=true` in `functions/.env` | Development helper (decided 2 Nov 2026). Creates or restores the fixed account `admin@mytester.com` / `1234567890`: Auth user enabled with that password, claims `{ roles: ["admin"], doctorId: null, branchIds: ["main"] }`, `users/{uid}` with `active: true`, `mustChangePassword: false`, `createdBy: "createTestAdmin"`; refresh tokens revoked so old sessions pick up the claims. Returns `{ uid, created }`. With the switch off it throws `failed-precondition`. Phase 9 sets the switch to false, redeploys and deletes the account. |
| `resetUserPassword` | callable, Admin only | Input `{ uid, temporaryPassword }` (min 8 chars). Sets the Auth password, sets `mustChangePassword: true`, revokes refresh tokens so the user must sign in again with the temporary password. |
| `assignPatientNo` | `patients` onCreate | Transaction: reads the patient and `counters/patients_{YY}` (YY = Karachi year of `createdAtLocal`, falling back to now), increments the counter and writes `patientNo` as `YY-NNNNN` plus `updatedAt: serverTimestamp()` (so reception delta pulls see the number, §9). Skips documents that already have a number, so a retried event never double-counts. |
| `applyDailySummaryDelta` | `visits`, `sales`, `expenses` onWrite | Computes before/after contribution and increments `dailySummaries/{date}` (see §4.22 delta rule). Zero reads. Skips duplicate events through `summaryEvents`. |
| `recomputeDay` | callable, Admin only | Repair tool: reads every visit, sale and expense of one `date` (a few hundred reads) and rewrites that summary from scratch. Used only when a total looks wrong. |
| `audit*` | onWrite on audited collections | Writes `auditLogs` with before, after, and changed fields. |
| `checkDuplicateFamilyPhone` | `families` onCreate | Queries `families` by the new family's phone; when more than one exists, sets `duplicatePhone: true` and `updatedAt: serverTimestamp()` on every one of them for Admin to merge (the stamp lets reception delta pulls see the flag, §9). |

Functions never write to collections that clients also write, except `patientNo`, `isFirstVisit` validation, the duplicate flag and `doctors.userId` (Admin-only, online-only data, so no offline conflict). This keeps offline writes free of conflicts.

---

## 6. Security Rules (summary)

Roles come from `request.auth.token.roles`. Helper functions: `isAdmin()`, `isReception()`, `isDoctor()`, `isOwnDoctor(doctorId)`.

| Collection | Read | Create | Update | Delete |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `branches`, `settings`, `departments`, `visitTypes`, `doctors` | any signed-in | Admin (`createdBy` = caller; `settings`: `updatedBy`) | Admin (`updatedBy` = caller). `doctors`: `userId`, `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` cannot change. Shape checks: non-empty names and codes, `salary` int ≥ 0, `sharePercent` 0–100, `shareBasis` in gross/net, `fees` map, boolean flags. `visitTypes`: a Doctor may change only `defaultPreOpChecklist` and `defaultPostOpDays` (+ `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`) of an operation type (Phase 5B) | never |
| `users` | own doc, or Admin | Functions only | Admin: only `displayName` (+ `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`). Owner: only `mustChangePassword` → `false` (+ `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`). Roles, `active`, `doctorId`: Functions only | never |
| `families`, `patients` | any signed-in | Reception, Admin (`createdBy` = caller, `branchId` in claims). `families`: non-empty `phone` and `headName`, `patientCount` int, `duplicatePhone == false`. `patients`: `patientNo == null`, non-empty `tempNo`, `familyId`, `name`, `gender` in male/female/other, `phones` and `searchKeys` lists, `visitCount` int, `deleted` bool | Reception, Admin (`updatedBy` = caller, same shape). Locked: `families.duplicatePhone`; `patients.patientNo`, `tempNo`; on both `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdAtLocal`, `createdBy` | never (soft) |
| `appointments` | any signed-in | Reception, Doctor, Admin (`createdBy` = caller, `branchId` in claims; non-empty `patientId`, `patientName`, `doctorId`, `date`; `status` in booked/arrived/cancelled/noShow; `source` in manual/followUp/postOp/operation) | Reception, Doctor, Admin (`updatedBy` = caller, same shape; `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` locked) | never |
| `visits` | any signed-in | Reception, Admin (shape in §4.11) | Admin any field except `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdAtLocal`, `createdBy`; Reception only `status`, `startedAt`, `completedAt` (+ `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`); Doctor the same three plus `hasPrescription`, on own visits only. `status` in waiting/inProgress/completed | never (soft) |
| `reports` | any signed-in | Reception, Admin (`createdBy`/`uploadedBy` = caller, `branchId` in claims; non-empty `patientId`, `title`, `storagePath`; `mimeType` in pdf/jpeg/png; `sizeBytes` int ≤ 10 MB; `deleted == false`) | Reception, Admin: `title`, or `deleted: true` with `deleteReason` (+ `deletedAt`, `deletedBy`, `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`); file fields, `patientId`, stamps locked | never (soft) |
| `operations` | any signed-in | Doctor, Admin (`createdBy` = caller, `branchId` in claims; non-empty `patientId`, `visitTypeId`, `surgeonDoctorId`, `scheduledDate`; `status == scheduled`; `checklist` and `postOpDays` lists) | Doctor, Admin: any business field (`status` in scheduled/done/cancelled; `done` needs `doneBy` and either `checklistComplete == true` or a non-empty `checklistOverrideReason` (rules cannot walk the list, so the client keeps the flag in step); `cancelled` needs `cancelReason`); Reception only `postOpDays`, `followUpAppointmentIds` (+ `updatedAt`, `updatedBy`); `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` locked | never |
| `prescriptions` | any signed-in | Doctor whose claim `doctorId` equals the visit's `doctorId` (one `get` on `visits/{visitId}`); document ID = `visitId` = `data.visitId`; `date` equals the visit's date; `createdBy` = caller; `branchId` in claims | The same doctor (`resource.data.doctorId`), only before the end of the prescription's Karachi day (§1); `visitId`, `patientId`, `doctorId`, `departmentId`, `date`, `branchId`, `createdAt`, `createdBy` locked; `updatedBy` = caller | never |
| `reports` | any signed-in | Reception, Admin | Reception, Admin | never (soft) |
| `operations` | any signed-in | Doctor, Admin | Doctor, Reception (only `postOpDays`, `followUpAppointmentIds`), Admin | never |
| `inventoryItems` | any signed-in | Admin | Admin; Reception only `stock` via increment | never |
| `suppliers`, `purchases` | Admin | Admin | Admin | never |
| `stockMovements` | Admin | Reception, Admin | never | never |
| `sales` | any signed-in | Reception, Admin | Admin | never (soft) |
| `expenses`, `payouts` | Admin | Admin | Admin | never |
| `dailySummaries`, `auditLogs`, `counters`, `summaryEvents` | Admin (`counters`, `summaryEvents`: nobody) | Functions | Functions | never |

Additional rule checks:
- Roles come from the ID token. After `setUserRoles` the client calls `getIdToken(true)`; the app does this automatically when the roles on the user document change.
- Callable error codes the app maps to messages: `unauthenticated`, `permission-denied`, `invalid-argument` (message names the field), `already-exists`, `not-found`, `failed-precondition`, `internal`.
- `branchId` must be in `request.auth.token.branchIds`.
- `createdBy` and `updatedBy` must equal `request.auth.uid`.
- `visits.discountAmount > 0` requires non-empty `discountReason`.
- `visits.netAmount == fee - discountAmount`.
- `deleted` may only be set to `true` by Admin with non-empty `deleteReason`.
- `dailySummaries` and `auditLogs` are read-only for clients.

## 7. Cloud Storage Layout

Bucket: the default bucket, created in `us-central1`.

```
clinic/logo.png
patients/{patientId}/reports/{reportId}.{pdf|jpg|png}
```
Rules: any signed-in user reads. Reception and Admin write under `reports` (Phase 5B: `patients/{patientId}/reports/{file}`, content type application/pdf, image/jpeg or image/png, max 10 MB, never deleted from the client); Admin writes `clinic/logo.png` (any `image/*` content type, max 2 MB, replaced in place; the download URL is stored in `settings.logoUrl`). Max 10 MB per report file. Report images are resized on the client to a maximum of 1200 px and JPEG quality 80 (roughly 150 KB) before upload so the 5 GB no-cost quota lasts years. The app points `firebase_storage` at the Storage emulator (port 9199) under `USE_EMULATORS=true`.

| `expenses` | `date asc, deleted asc` |

Firestore will also prompt for any missing index on first use; the list above is the expected set.

## 9. Offline Strategy (Reception Web)

- Firestore persistence is enabled with `persistentLocalCache`, unlimited size, multi-tab manager on web (a second Chrome tab shares the IndexedDB cache instead of falling back to memory), client-side index auto-creation on, and `web/index.html` calls `navigator.storage.persist()` so Chrome treats the cache as durable. The cache is keyed by site, not by login: it survives tab close, Chrome restart and signing out and in again. It is lost by "Clear browsing data", incognito windows, another Chrome profile or PC.
- On login reception attaches live listeners to: `settings`, `departments`, `doctors`, `visitTypes`, `inventoryItems`, today's `visits`, today's and tomorrow's `appointments`. **Patients and families are not listened to and not downloaded up front** (decided 5 Nov 2026, replacing the full-collection listeners that Firestore re-billed in full after every disconnect longer than 30 minutes). Instead:
  - **Local-first search.** `PatientSearchViewModel` runs every phone, number and name lookup against the cache first (`ReadSource.cache`, zero reads). Only when the cache has no match does it repeat the query on the server (`ReadSource.server`, billed per document returned), and those documents then live in the cache. Families of the matched patients are read the same way. A phone search expects the whole family, so when the cache returns fewer members than the family's `patientCount` the search is repeated on the server (a single cached member, for example one pulled by the watermark seed or opened from a visit, must not hide the rest). A footer "Not here? Search online" (`search-online`) under cached results forces a server search when the patient wanted is not among them. Offline, a cache miss shows "Search failed" with the offline message, since a patient this device has never seen cannot be found without the server.
  - **Delta sync.** `PatientSyncController` runs while a reception user is signed in: on a device's first run it stores the server's newest `updatedAt` per collection (`patientSync.patients`, `patientSync.families` in `KeyValueStore`; one read each, or the clock when the collection is empty); at every sign-in and every 5 minutes it pulls `patients` and `families` with `updatedAt >= watermark` ordered by `updatedAt, __name__` in pages of 500 from the server, so every document touched anywhere in the clinic since the last pull (new patients, numbers assigned by the trigger, visit counters, phone changes, duplicate flags) refreshes the cache, then stores the newest `updatedAt` seen. A pull that fails (offline) keeps the watermark and retries on the next tick. A query that returns nothing is still one billed read, so the idle cost is about 2 reads per 5 minutes per device.
- Writes go to the local cache first and sync in the background. The UI shows an online/offline badge and a pending-write count. Decided 4 Nov 2026: both come from the today's-visits listener (`includeMetadataChanges: true`): the count is the number of today's visit documents with `hasPendingWrites`, and the badge shows Offline while the latest snapshot `isFromCache` with nothing pending. No extra listener, no polling.
- New patients get `tempNo` immediately; `patientNo` arrives after sync and the next receipt shows it.
- Firestore resolves a write's future only when the server has acknowledged it, so an awaited `commit()` would hang Save while offline. Decided 4 Nov 2026: repositories wrap every reception write in `commitOrQueue` (`core/firebase/offline_write.dart`), which waits up to 1.5 s for the acknowledgement (so a rules rejection still surfaces online) and otherwise returns, treating the write as queued in the local cache. A rejection that arrives later is logged; the document disappears from the listener, which is the visible sign.
- Doctors and admins without the reception role do not run the delta sync, but their searches are local-first too, so a patient opened twice on a phone costs one read, not two.
- The today's-visits listener (`visits where date == today`) is held by `TodayVisitsController` (Phase 4) for reception and admin sessions and re-subscribes when the Karachi date changes. The Visits list, the queue board, the shift summary, the sync badge and the "waiting now" count on the new-visit form all read from it, so a day of 500 visits costs about 500 reads per reception device. Phase 5A: for a session that has the doctor role but neither reception nor admin, the same controller listens to `visits where doctorId == mine and date == today` instead, so a doctor's phone pays only for their own visits; the doctor queue reads from it.
- Tokens are computed from the cache. Receipt PDFs are generated on the client, so printing works offline.
- Uploads (reports) are queued by the app and sent when online; the report document is created only after the file upload succeeds.

## 10. Seed Data

The first Admin user is created with the Firebase console (or the dev test-admin button). While `settings/general` is missing, every Admin page shows a banner leading to `/admin/setup` (decided 3 Nov 2026: banner, not a forced redirect). The Initial setup screen asks for the clinic name, address and phone and writes in one batch: `branches/main`, `settings/general` (defaults from §4.2), departments Eye and Homeopathy, visit types Checkup and Follow-up for each plus Eye Test (fixed IDs, §4.4 and §4.6, merged so a re-run never duplicates). The emulator seed (`functions/scripts/seed-emulator.js`) writes the same catalog IDs plus, since Phase 5B, the operation type `eye-cataract` (Cataract Surgery, checklist Blood sugar and Consent signed, post-op days 1, 7, 30, fee 25,000 on the seed doctor), one doctor, a plain reception account (`reception@clinic.test` / `Reception12345`) and one family (`03001234567`, Khan) with two patients, and deliberately leaves `settings/general` missing so the integration test covers the setup screen.

## 11. Cost Expectations

Target: stay inside the Blaze no-cost quotas. Re-sized 5 Nov 2026 (owner's figures) for **500 visits a day: 300 new patients and 200 returning patients**, about 200 new families, 50 report uploads, 10 operations, 10 doctors on phones, 2 reception PCs and one Admin screen. Phases 6 to 8 (appointments, sales, stock, summaries) are not built yet and are estimated separately in the last row.

| Resource | Daily use at 500 visits | No-cost quota | Monthly cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Firestore reads | about 22,000: today's-visits listeners (3 whole-day screens, each visit changes 3 to 4 times, plus doctors' own queues and phone re-opens) 9,500; patient delta pulls on 2 PCs (about 1,000 changed documents a day plus 2 polls every 5 minutes) 2,500; searches (cache misses, the phone check before each registration) 1,600 at first and under 1,000 once the cache has warmed; new-visit form 1,000; doctor consultations (visit, prescription, patient history, see below) 3,800; patient pages at reception 2,000; receipt and visit pages 500; Function triggers 1,000; catalog, settings and summary aggregates 300 | 50,000 / day | 0 |
| Firestore writes | about 5,000: 300 new patients and 200 families (patient, family counter, numbering trigger) 1,400; 500 visits (create, patient counter, start, prescription, completion, follow-up appointment) 3,500; operations and reports 100 | 20,000 / day | 0 |
| Firestore storage incl. indexes | about 4 MB a day, 120 MB a month, 1.4 GiB a year (about 110,000 new patients a year with their `searchKeys` index entries) | 1 GiB | 0 for about 8 months, then about 0.10 to 0.20 USD a month in year 1, growing by that much each year |
| Cloud Functions | about 500 invocations (300 `assignPatientNo`, 200 `checkDuplicateFamilyPhone`, a few callables) | 2,000,000 / month | 0 |
| Cloud Storage (us-central1) | reports about 10 MB a day (images shrunk to 1200 px), 300 MB a month | 5 GB stored, 1 GB download / day | 0 for about 16 months, then about 0.02 USD per GB stored |
| Hosting, Auth, App Check | small | generous | 0 |
| Phases 6 to 8 (estimate) | appointments 200 reads and writes, sales and stock about 300 writes, summaries about 1,000 trigger invocations and writes | within the above | 0 |

Expected bill: 0 USD for the first eight months, well under 1 USD a month through year two. The quota is per day, so one unusual day matters more than the monthly average; reads have about 2x headroom. Things that would break the target and are therefore not in the design: full-day recompute of summaries, nightly full exports, photo prescriptions, a Mumbai Storage bucket, live listeners over whole collections.

**Doctor history reads, the item that grows with time.** Opening a consultation (`ConsultationViewModel`) subscribes to the visit, its prescription, and the patient's every visit, prescription and operation (`watchPatientVisits`, `watchPatientPrescriptions`, `watchPatientOperations`, no limit). A new patient costs about 4 reads; a returning patient costs 3 plus two reads per past visit (the visit and its prescription), so 13 at 5 past visits and 63 at 30. The reception patient page (`PatientDetailViewModel`) opens the same visits and prescriptions lists. At today's mix (200 returning patients averaging 5 past visits) this is about 3,800 reads a day; when chronic patients reach 30 visits it becomes about 13,000 and is the first item to push a busy day past the quota. Planned fix, not yet built: load the latest 10 visits and prescriptions (`orderBy date desc, limit 10`, composite indexes on `patientId` + `date` for `visits` and `prescriptions`) and fetch the rest only when the doctor opens the History tab.

A new reception device downloads nothing up front: its cache fills from searches and delta pulls. Revised 5 Nov 2026: the earlier design (full `patients` and `families` listeners, searches on the server) was measured against Firestore's billing rules and would have cost 20,000 to 90,000 reads a day in searches plus a full re-read of both collections per reception device after every disconnect longer than 30 minutes (Firestore bills a resumed listener as a new query after that), which is why it was replaced by the local-first search and delta sync in §9.

---

## 12. Open Points

1. If a second reception device is ever added, token generation must move to a transaction or a Function. Not needed in v1.
2. Firestore storage passes the 1 GiB no-cost quota during year 1 at 500 visits a day. Cost is cents; if it matters, drop unused composite indexes or shorten `searchKeys`.
3. Firestore cannot search by substring. Name search uses prefix keys; "contains" search would require Algolia or Typesense later.
